Each slot's start callable reads the loop variable when called, so every slot runs the last job in the batch.
All grid rows are the same list, so a batch longer than one row shows only the last row's jobs in every row.
Defaults are copied shallowly, so a nested override changes the handler's registered defaults and later jobs' options.
Jobs are removed from the list being walked, so the job right after each removed one is skipped and finished jobs stay queued.
Every exception is treated as retryable, so a non-retryable error is retried and then swallowed instead of reaching the caller.
all() is true for an empty list, so an empty batch counts as succeeded.
